metadata.comment: `rowClass` rather than an `archived` boolean the row turns into a class: which class this row wears is a fact about the coach's list, and Logic/Standing owns it. An archived dimension is quieter and never struck through.

nodes.label: What they agreed to get better at

metadata.comment: The coach's own words, in INK — never the series colour (the dataviz rule). This is what makes a small multiple work: identity is in the text, so four rows need no legend and no four colours that nearly work.

nodes.label: Where they are against the goal

metadata.comment: The kit draws; Logic/Standing measured. Every position arrives as a fraction of the same 1-10 track, so two dimensions with different targets are read against ONE ruler — two tracks scaled to their own targets would make a 4-against-5 and a 9-against-10 look identical, which is the thing a gauge exists to stop.
